question.text: For electron in ' 2 s ' and ' 2 p ' orbitals, the orbital angular momentum values, respectively are :

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Orbital angular momentum }=\sqrt{\ell(\ell+1)} \frac{\mathrm{h}}{2 \pi} \\ & \therefore \quad \text { For } 2 \mathrm{~s} \text { orbital }: \ell=0 \\ & \text { Orbital angular momentum }=0 \\ & \therefore \quad \text { For } 2 \mathrm{p} \text { orbital }: \ell=1 \\ & \quad \begin{aligned} \text { Orbital angular momentum } & =\sqrt{1(1+2)} \frac{\mathrm{h}}{2 \pi} \\ & =\sqrt{2} \frac{\mathrm{~h}}{2 \pi}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}$
